whatTheyArgued: Per secondary sources: Die neue Typographie (1928) was a modernist rulebook that favoured sans-serif type, asymmetric non-centred layouts and clear functional hierarchy. From about 1932 Tschichold abandoned its rigidity, later called it too extreme and compared its dogmatism to authoritarian politics. At Penguin (1947-49) he set the Penguin Composition Rules, a house standard drawing on classical book conventions (serif faces, centred title pages), which contradict the 1928 manifesto. The Form of the Book (essays 1949-74) argues for tradition, legibility and balance. None of these concern reading a text's setting to separate edition from author, or declaring a frame.

ourUse: tschichold.js reads how a text was set (wraps, lineation, labels, running heads, page UI, doubled fetches) from bytes, learns rules once from originals, and declares the setting as a frame via frame.js before readings are compared, so edition conventions are not mistaken for authorial facts. Closed typographic grammar is stated as tables.

bends.ours: 'A text's setting is read and declared before its words are'; typography read as evidence about an edition.
bends.theirs: Tschichold argued how to compose a page so form serves function and readers; he did not argue for reading received bytes to peel off edition artefacts. The kinship (conventions as a compositor's craft the reader should not have to notice) is real but the discipline is ours.

bends.ours: Credit pairs Die neue Typographie (1928) with 'a page's form answers to its function' as the lineage for convention-reading.
bends.theirs: The 1928 book is the doctrine he later repudiated; the convention-codifying work is the Penguin Composition Rules and The Form of the Book. The compendium cites the repudiated work as the source for a house-conventions stance.

bends.ours: Applied to digital text bytes, OCR, Wikisource wikitext, GRETIL e-texts in Arabic, Chinese, Greek and IAST.
bends.theirs: His rules are for printed Latin-script books; Penguin rules assume English composition. The non-Latin extension is entirely ours.

bends.ours: Handle line and role name him for a measurement organ (rules with evidence and falsification, bench priors).
bends.theirs: The measured-rule machinery, p-value bars and CV look are not typographic doctrine.
